name: discovery
title: Discovery & Foundations
description: Foundational discovery for newer or larger projects, especially rebuilds of an existing site. Creates a single Discovery / Foundation task list with a Feature per area (access, goals, current site audit, SEO, analytics, technical, content and IA), ending in a findings playback and a sign-off milestone. Tasks marked High priority capture things that are gone for good once the old site is switched off - never skip those on a rebuild.

variables.name: current_domain
variables.description: The existing site's domain being audited, e.g. example.com

tasks.title: Access & Accounts
tasks.description: Get the access discovery depends on. Requests are due five days after the template is applied - discovery stalls without them.

subtasks.title: Request Google Search Console access
subtasks.description: Ask the client to add TSD as a Full user on the Search Console property for {{current_domain}}. If no property exists, set one up **now** - Search Console only holds data from the day it's verified, so every day's delay is a day of lost baseline.

subtasks.title: Request GA4 and GTM access
subtasks.description: Editor on GA4 and Publish on GTM. If the site has no GA4 at all, note it - the analytics baseline tasks become 'set up tracking now so there's something to compare against'.

subtasks.title: Request current CMS admin access
subtasks.description: Needed for the content inventory, forms audit and to see how the current site is actually managed.

subtasks.title: Establish who controls the domain, DNS and hosting
subtasks.description: Find out who holds the domain registration, the DNS and the current hosting for {{current_domain}}, and either get access or a named contact who can make changes. This is the most common late go-live blocker - find out in week one, not launch week. Record it in the TSD domain list.

tasks.title: Goals & Stakeholders
tasks.description: Understand what the client needs the site to achieve, for whom, and how success will be measured.

subtasks.title: Stakeholder interviews
subtasks.description: Understand the business goals, frustrations with the current site, internal processes, and who signs off what.

subtasks.title: Define goals and success KPIs
subtasks.description: Agree measurable goals (enquiries, sales, organic traffic, etc) and tie each one to a baseline captured during discovery, so success can be shown after launch.

subtasks.title: Audiences and key user journeys
subtasks.description: Identify the primary audiences and the top journeys each needs to complete. Feeds the information architecture and the QA test plans.

subtasks.title: Competitor review
subtasks.description: Review 3-5 competitor sites for features, content and positioning. Note what to adopt and what to avoid.

tasks.title: Current Site Audit
tasks.description: Crawl and inventory the existing site so nothing is lost in the rebuild: every URL, template, broken link and linked document.

subtasks.title: Screaming Frog crawl of the current site
subtasks.description:
Full crawl of https://{{current_domain}}.

Before crawling:
* Check with the client whether a WAF/CDN will block or rate-limit the crawler (whitelist the IP or lower the crawl speed)
* Enable JavaScript rendering if the site is JS-heavy
* Add the XML sitemap(s) as a crawl source so orphan pages are picked up

Save the crawl file and these exports to the project folder: Internal (all), Response Codes, Redirects, Page Titles, Meta Descriptions, H1, Canonicals, Images missing alt text.

subtasks.title: Build the full legacy URL inventory
subtasks.description:
A crawl alone misses orphan pages. Merge into one spreadsheet:
* Crawl URLs
* XML sitemap URLs
* Search Console top pages (last 16 months)
* GA4 landing pages with traffic
* Top backlinked URLs

This is the source list for the redirect map - any URL missing here becomes a 404 after launch.

subtasks.title: Document the current sitemap and page templates
subtasks.description: Group the inventory by section and page template (e.g. 40 case studies, 120 news articles, 12 service pages). This gives the page-type list for the build and the volumes for content migration estimates.

subtasks.title: Record broken links, redirect chains and errors
subtasks.description: From the crawl: 4xx/5xx pages, internal links pointing at redirects, redirect chains and loops. Fix these going forward in the new site rather than carrying them over.

subtasks.title: Inventory documents and media with inbound links
subtasks.description: PDFs and other files on the old site often have inbound links and search traffic of their own. List them (Screaming Frog > Internal > PDF, plus Search Console) so they're migrated or redirected rather than silently dropped.

subtasks.title: Archive the current site
subtasks.description: Screenshot the key pages and templates for before/after comparison and the portfolio, and keep the crawl file. Once DNS switches, the old site is gone.

tasks.title: SEO Baseline
tasks.description: Record where the site stands in search today, so post-launch performance can be judged against it.

subtasks.title: Export the Search Console performance baseline
subtasks.description: Export the last 16 months of queries and pages (clicks, impressions, CTR, average position). This is the benchmark post-launch performance is judged against - and the evidence if the 'we've fallen off Google' conversation ever happens.

subtasks.title: Record the keyword ranking baseline
subtasks.description: Agree the handful of keywords that matter to the client (usually location + service terms) and record current positions in the rank tracker. Start weekly tracking now, so there's a pre-launch trend rather than a single data point.

subtasks.title: Review the backlink profile and top linked pages
subtasks.description: Using Search Console's Links report (plus Ahrefs/Semrush if available), list the most-linked pages. Each must redirect to its best equivalent on the new site - losing them loses the authority they carry.

subtasks.title: Check indexation and crawl directives
subtasks.description: Compare indexed pages (Search Console > Pages) with the inventory. Note noindex pages, robots.txt rules, canonical tags and any hreflang. Anything deliberately hidden today should stay hidden on the new site.

subtasks.title: Record the Core Web Vitals and PageSpeed baseline
subtasks.description: Run the key templates through PageSpeed Insights and note the Search Console Core Web Vitals report. Gives a before/after for the performance story at launch.

subtasks.title: Note structured data and rich results in use
subtasks.description: Check the key templates with Google's Rich Results Test (Organisation, Product, Article, FAQ, Breadcrumb etc). Any rich results the site earns today must be preserved.

tasks.title: Analytics & Tracking
tasks.description: Record current traffic and conversions, and everything that tracks visitors, so it can all be carried over.

subtasks.title: Export the analytics traffic baseline
subtasks.description: From GA4: sessions, users, top landing pages, channels and conversions for the last 12 months. Pairs with the Search Console export as the post-launch benchmark.

subtasks.title: Audit the conversions and events that must be preserved
subtasks.description: List every GA4 key event and what it measures (form submissions, purchases, downloads, phone clicks). Each one needs re-implementing and testing on the new site.

subtasks.title: Inventory third-party scripts and tracking pixels
subtasks.description: Check GTM and the page source for everything that fires: Meta Pixel, LinkedIn Insight, Google Ads conversion tags, Clarity/Hotjar, chat widgets, review widgets. These are routinely forgotten on a relaunch, and the client's marketing team only notices when campaign reporting breaks.

subtasks.title: Review the cookie consent setup
subtasks.description: Note the current consent platform (e.g. Cookiebot, CookieYes), which scripts it controls, and whether Google Consent Mode v2 is configured. The new site needs parity or better.

tasks.title: Technical & Integrations
tasks.description: Document the current platform, hosting, DNS and every connected system.

subtasks.title: Document the current platform and hosting
subtasks.description: CMS/platform and version, hosting provider, CDN/WAF, SSL, licences in use, and any custom functionality that must be replicated.

subtasks.title: Integrations inventory
subtasks.description: Every system the site talks to: CRM, email marketing, payments, stock/ERP, booking, search, SSO, APIs. For each, record what data flows which way, who owns the account, and whether credentials or API access are available.

subtasks.title: Snapshot the DNS zone and email records
subtasks.description: Export the current DNS zone for {{current_domain}}: MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, verification TXT records and subdomains. A DNS move that drops any of these takes the client's email or a third-party service down on launch day.

subtasks.title: Accessibility baseline
subtasks.description: Automated scan of the key templates (axe or WAVE) to record the starting point, and confirm any compliance requirement (e.g. WCAG 2.2 AA for public sector clients).

subtasks.title: Security and compliance requirements
subtasks.description: GDPR and data retention, PCI scope if taking payments, penetration testing requirements, and any sector-specific obligations.

tasks.title: Content & Information Architecture
tasks.description: Decide what content moves, how the new site is structured, and how every old URL maps to a new one.

subtasks.title: Content audit (keep / merge / rewrite / remove)
subtasks.description: Using the page inventory, agree the fate of each page or section with the client. This drives both the new sitemap and the migration effort.

subtasks.title: Proposed sitemap and information architecture
subtasks.description: Draft the new site structure and navigation from the content audit and key user journeys, for client sign-off. The signed-off sitemap becomes the page-type list for the build (the tsd-site-scaffold skill can turn it into build tickets).

subtasks.title: Agree the content migration approach and ownership
subtasks.description: Who writes, who migrates, manual or scripted, and by when. Content is the most common cause of a slipped launch date - agree it now, in writing.

subtasks.title: Forms inventory
subtasks.description: Every form on the current site: its fields, where submissions go (inbox, CRM, email marketing tool), auto-responders and spam protection. Each needs rebuilding with the same destination.

subtasks.title: Draft the redirect map (old URL to new URL)
subtasks.description: Once the new sitemap is signed off, map every URL in the legacy inventory to its new equivalent, or the closest relevant page - never a blanket redirect to the homepage. Finalised and tested before go-live.

tasks.title: Discovery findings report and playback
tasks.description: Write up the findings, baselines, recommendations and risks, and play them back to the client.

tasks.title: Discovery sign-off
tasks.description: Milestone: the client has signed off the discovery findings, sitemap and scope, and the build can be planned from them.
